title: What If Earth Always Showed the Same Face to the Sun?

scenes.text: What if Earth always faced the Sun with the same side? One half would never see night.
That is tidal locking, the same trick that makes the Moon show Earth only one face.
A locked planet has a permanent day side and a permanent night side.
Models show ice spreading from the day-night edge across the night side.
Near the point facing the star, the seas could stay liquid, hottest at the center of the eye.
Closer to its star, the ice would thaw into a water world. Farther out, it would freeze into an iceball.

description:
What if Earth always faced the Sun with the same side?
Scientists call these worlds eyeball planets: an icy night side, and an ocean on the day side facing the star.
What should we run through next?
